solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Union supporter trips in British Museum — help needed

indicators.note: the trips are placed inside the abbreviation for the museum

parts.note: BM is the standard abbreviation for the British Museum in London
trips on horseback or in a car are rides
help or assistance is aid

explanation.surface: A trade unionist stumbles inside the British Museum and needs assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but here it is a marriage, and the supporter is the bride's attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a union, and the attendant who supports the bride at it fills exactly that role.

clue.text: Hear pal has become a painter

indicators.note: the letters of the two words turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A friend you overhear has taken up painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Renaissance master of Urbino is one of the most famous painters in history.

clue.text: King comes in late for quail

indicators.note: the king's letter enters the word for late, sitting inside it

parts.note: the late, i.e. deceased, are dead
R, from Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch arrives late for a game bird dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quail' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to shrink in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to cower or recoil in fear, which is what it means to feel terror of something.

clue.text: Suffer gentle slap but refuse to change

parts.note: to suffer or tolerate something is to stand it
a pat is a light tap with the hand

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with a light smack but will not budge.
explanation.walkthrough: To stand pat is an idiom from poker: keep the hand you hold, refusing to draw new cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means holding firm to a position and declining any alteration.

clue.text: Once more measure refuse reluctantly

parts.note: once more means again
a stone is a British measure of weight, fourteen pounds
swill is kitchen refuse or slops fed to pigs

explanation.surface: A grudging person measures out rubbish one more time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun for waste; a stone is a British unit of body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with unwillingness, under protest, is doing it in that grudging manner.

clue.text: Duke has loads of fantasies

parts.note: reams, like loads, means a great quantity

explanation.surface: A nobleman has a great many daydreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasies and imaginings of the sleeping or waking mind are synonyms.

clue.text: Fish for fingerprints

definitions.meaning: a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flatfish species and, in British slang, prints taken from fingers.

clue.text: Stunt man died? That's a ruddy disaster!

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died in records and family trees
ruddy means red in colour
an evil is a misfortune or calamity

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a stuntman's death is a bloody catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruddy' works in the surface as a mild British swear word but gives its colour sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless person who performs dangerous feats, such as a stunt performer, is a fearless risk-taker.

clue.text: It is played to keep fool in favour

indicators.note: the word for favour holds the fool inside it

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone plays along to keep a fool in good graces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' suggests a game or trick; it is an instrument, the woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: The low-pitched double-reed woodwind is a musical instrument, something one plays.

clue.text: Primate holds beginning of service in church

indicators.note: the primate contains the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: the first letter of the word service is taken

explanation.surface: A monkey attends the opening of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The vaulted semicircular recess at the east end is a feature found in a church building.

clue.text: The samurai becomes incompetent

indicators.note: the letters of the warrior phrase change into a new word, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A Japanese warrior loses his skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done without professional skill, clumsy and unpolished, is inexpert or incompetent.

clue.text: John worked for Frank

parts.note: a john is slang for a toilet, as is can
did, as in did a job, means worked

explanation.surface: A man named John worked for a man named Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' and 'Frank' look like names; one is slang for a lavatory, the other means honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and open, speaking without hiding anything, are synonyms for being honest.

clue.text: Trying to impress improperly? Pardon me!

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the verb for doing this by citing famous acquaintances

indicators.note: the letters of the apology are arranged in an improper order

explanation.surface: Someone apologises after showing off in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention famous acquaintances casually is a way of seeking to dazzle listeners.

clue.text: Witchcraft leads to shortage in pub by Tuesday

indicators.note: the shortage goes inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: Sorcery is blamed for a pub running short on a Tuesday.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes sorcery or magic used for evil ends, the dark arts.

clue.text: Compositions arranged? No chance, son!

indicators.note: the letters are arranged, as music is arranged, into new order

explanation.surface: Asked whether his compositions have been arranged, a father says no chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' doubles as a musical term in the surface; 'No' is only part of the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaconne is a musical piece built over a repeated bass, so these are compositions.

clue.text: Very last trade

parts.note: the end is the last part

explanation.surface: A dealer's final transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell goods, especially from a stall or machine, is to trade in them.

clue.text: Small knife I bought initially for cut of meat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a parer is a small knife for peeling

indicators.note: only the opening letter of bought is taken

explanation.surface: Someone buys a little knife to prepare a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib of pork with most of the meat trimmed off is a familiar butcher's cut.

clue.text: Caught in flagrante delicto in India

indicators.note: the letters are caught inside the word flagrante

explanation.surface: Someone is caught red-handed in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of the Taj Mahal lies in the north of India, in Uttar Pradesh.

clue.text: Noble fellow experienced festivity in the first place

indicators.note: the festivity is put at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
had, as in had a good time, means experienced

explanation.surface: A noble man had a party at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Galahad is the purest knight of the Round Table, so the name stands for any noble fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian knight is a byword for chivalry and virtue, an honourable man.

clue.text: Asian has fence going in two directions

indicators.note: the fence goes inside the pair of compass points

parts.note: NE and SE, northeast and southeast, are two compass directions
a pale is a fence stake, or a fence made of stakes

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia owns a fence running two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Himalayan kingdom is an Asian by nationality.

clue.text: Underwear makes one tense

parts.note: single means one
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Underwear causes someone to feel nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: A singlet is the British term for a sleeveless vest worn under a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The sleeveless vest is an undergarment in British usage.

clue.text: Celebrity went ahead without the facts

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside: the led piece surrounds the facts

parts.note: led means went in front
gen is British slang for information, the facts

explanation.surface: A famous figure acted without knowing the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous person admired over a long time is called a living icon, a star.

clue.text: Underwear displayed in bed

definitions.meaning: flowers that bloom in a flower bed are, whimsically, things that bloom

explanation.definitionFit: The word names old-fashioned baggy knickers and also plants flowering in a garden bed.

clue.text: Reprimand sailor

definitions.meaning: a naval sailor without a commission

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scolding and an ordinary seaman below officer rank.

clue.text: Narrow strip on bit of road

parts.note: a tape is a narrow strip of material

indicators.note: a bit, the first letter, of the word road is taken

explanation.surface: A thin strip lies on a stretch of road.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to become gradually thinner towards one end, to narrow.

clue.text: Ornament broken? Cleaner hid!

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are broken up and put together differently

explanation.surface: A cleaner hides after breaking a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative hanging light with branched holders is an ornamental fixture.

clue.text: Limit for writer drinking port

indicators.note: the writer takes in the port, swallowing it

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
port is the left side of a ship, abbreviated L

explanation.surface: A writer has a limit on how much port he drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine but is the ship's left side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole is an extreme, as in poles apart, the furthest point or limit.

clue.text: Oscar gets some French poetry

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
des is French for some

explanation.surface: Oscar acquires a few French poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests Wilde, but is just the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject are a form of poetry.

clue.text: Considered giving shop censure

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop
to berate is to scold or censure

explanation.surface: A thoughtful decision to criticise a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something considered is done on purpose after careful thought, intentional.
